title: Carry a checked exception through a Function

blocks.text: `Function.apply` declares no checked exceptions, so a method such as one that reads a file cannot be used as a `Function` directly. The usual answer is a custom functional interface whose one method declares `throws Exception`, plus a helper that adapts it to a standard `Function`.
The file declares `CheckedFunction<T, R>` (method `R apply(T t) throws Exception`) and the unchecked `ApplyFailedException(String message, Throwable cause)`. Write two static methods of `Checked`:

items: `<T, R> Function<T, R> unchecked(CheckedFunction<T, R> function)` returns a `Function` that applies `function`; when it throws any exception, the `Function` throws an `ApplyFailedException` with the message `"failed on " + input` instead.
`<T, R> List<R> mapAll(List<T> inputs, CheckedFunction<T, R> function)` applies `function` to each input in order and returns the results, failing the same way.

blocks.text: Whoever catches the `ApplyFailedException` needs to know what really went wrong, and a failure means the remaining inputs are not worth trying.

cases.says: A function that does not fail gives its ordinary results, one by one and over a list.
The unchecked wrapper keeps the original exception as its cause and names the input.
mapAll stops at the first failing input and never applies the function to the rest.

concepts: A custom interface whose method declares throws Exception carries checked exceptions, and a wrapper adapts it to Function.
